Dear colleagues,

The Berkeley Research Academy is starting several new research projects over the coming weeks with mentors from around the world. We welcome students and researchers to join, and I've prepared a list of Lean-related projects below. Further projects are possible provided we find suitable mentors. The projects include individualized research management and offer awards to successful participants. This is not an official UC Berkeley program. Feel free to reach out with any questions regarding the research topics and procedure. Register at jasper.kreeke@berkeley.edu.

Kontsevich Deformation Quantization in Lean
Mentored by Erik Herrera. Other participants and project manager TBD.
This project aims to formalize Kontsevich’s deformation quantization theorem in the Lean theorem prover. The theorem gives a universal procedure for deforming the algebra of functions on a Poisson manifold into a noncommutative algebra, building a deep bridge between geometry, topology, and mathematical physics. The project will involve formalizing parts of Poisson geometry, graph-based constructions, and configuration-space integrals, while exploring how advanced geometric ideas can be represented inside Lean.

Understanding the Expressivity of Multi-Headed Attention
Mentored by Karthik Viswanathan. Other participants and project manager TBD.
This project studies the expressive power of multi-headed attention, one of the central building blocks of modern transformers. The guiding question is surprisingly concrete: how many attention heads are required to compute a given Boolean function? Initial results show that parity on n bits requires exactly n heads, while functions such as AND and OR require only one. The project aims to extend this analysis to broader classes of Boolean functions and develop a general complexity theory for attention mechanisms. Alongside the mathematics, the project will build a Lean-based “mech-interp dojo”: a formalized environment in which coding agents and human researchers collaborate on theorem proving and mechanistic interpretability. Participants will work at the intersection of transformer theory, Boolean complexity, formal verification, and AI-assisted mathematics.

Singular Value Decomposition in Lean
Currently working on this project: Niels Voss, Robert Ho. With help of a PhD student in functional analysis and mentored by Jasper.
Singular Value Decompositions (SVD) are a standard decomposition of matrices M = UΣV* where U and V are complex unitary matrices and Σ is a rectangular diagonal matrix with nonnegative real numbers on the diagonal. This project aims to implement SVD in the Lean theorem prover for use in Mathlib. The mathematical side of this project is linear algebra and thus undergraduate material. However, SVDs are non-unique and it has turned out that the first step consists of finding a canonical way to state SVDs without many choices. After this is accomplished, the canonical presentation will be implemented in Lean.

Thanks you all for registering! We are looking for more managers to get all these projects off the ground.
1) Managers. We are looking for individuals with a talent for managing people and some Lean/research experience. Your role will be to move projects forward by focusing their contributors on performance. Expertise is not required.
2) Stipends. Management is suitable as a part-time activity. The academy offers awards and possibly monthly stipends for excellent managers. Final determination is at the discretion of the academy.
3) Logistics. Fully remote. Not an official UC Berkeley program. Feel free to inquire with any questions regarding the role and expectations. Register at jasper.kreeke@berkeley.edu.

Dear Lean community,

The academy is starting a new round of projects. We have upgraded our research management with full-time research manager Fahad Sarwar, who is currently managing up to 10 projects and would be happy to take on more. Respond to jasper.kreeke@berkeley.edu.

We are looking for
• project proposals for new projects. Send us a project title, short abstract, missing expertise (if additional mentors with complementary expertise are required). The academy will recruit project participants.
• existing projects to be managed by the academy. If you are currently supervising large projects, this is an exceptional service free of cost, serving to test our management-based research system. You will continue mentoring and owning the projects scientifically.

1) Subjects. We are interested in projects from pure mathematics to math/Lean/AI, including large-scale formalization efforts and experimental AI-assisted theorem proving.
2) Aim. The mathematics projects serve to demonstrate the superiority of our research management model over academia. The math/Lean/AI projects additionally serve to demonstrate the effectiveness of matching mathematicians with AI engineers. The goal is to reduce supervision load for mentors by up to 75%, while increasing researcher engagement.
3) Your role. Academy projects are run by professional managers. They have research experience but lack domain expertise. Your role as mentor is to fill this gap. The academy strictly aims to keep the mentoring load per project around 1 hour every 3 weeks.

Best wishes,
Jasper
